fair_value.method: Sum of the parts on ~3.95B shares: core auto (~$120B 2027 revenue, ~6% normalized net margin, ~$7B x 30 = ~$240B, ~$60/sh) + energy storage (~$3B EBIT x 25 = ~$75B, ~$19/sh) + FSD software (~3M subs, ~$120B, ~$30/sh) + probability-weighted robotaxi network (~$500B, ~$125/sh) + probability-weighted Optimus (~$250B, ~$65/sh) + net cash and SpaceX stake (~$30B, ~$8/sh) = ~$307, rounded up to $320 because the market has long paid a premium for Musk-led optionality. As a cross-check, 2027 consensus EPS of ~$2.68 at 120x gives ~$320.

bear.story: Capex of more than $25B/yr keeps FCF negative through 2027; auto margins slide further as regulatory credits disappear and competition from BYD and others bites; the NHTSA Cybercab audit forces a recertification or pause; robotaxi growth stays slow; the EU FSD vote slips; 2027 EPS comes in under $2; the multiple compresses toward 80-100x forward earnings.

base.story: Deliveries grow modestly (~1.8-1.9M in 2027) and energy keeps growing. Robotaxi spreads to more US metros and whole states and Cybercab volume ramps slowly. FSD is approved in more EU countries. Optimus is still in the flat early part of its S-curve. FCF gets close to breakeven in late 2027, and the stock trades roughly flat inside a wide range, still valued on autonomy optionality.

bull.story: Robotaxi scales visibly (thousands of Cybercabs in fleet sales, unsupervised service in many states), FSD wins EU-wide and China approval, Optimus shows external deployments, and a SpaceX/xAI combination or AI narrative re-rates the stock back to or above its $498 high.

thesis_break_reason: About 29% below the current price and clearly under the $297 52-week low and the July 2026 capitulation low of ~$304. A sustained trade there would most likely mean the autonomy story has been damaged (a regulatory halt of Cybercab/robotaxi operations, a serious safety incident, or EU/China FSD rejections) or that the core business has broken (auto margins in single digits with FCF burn running above plan). It would not be ordinary 46%-vol noise around a flat base case.

key_uncertainties: Whether a Tesla-SpaceX merger happens before the horizon and at what exchange ratio (analysts cite 80-90% odds by early 2027). This could drive a large jump in either direction or change the security itself
The pace of robotaxi/Cybercab scaling and the regulatory outcome of the NHTSA certification audit
How long FCF stays negative with capex above $25B/yr, and whether auto margins keep falling after Q2's 16.3% auto GM (ex-credits) and 1.4% operating margin
Timing of EU-wide and China FSD approvals
Optimus commercialization timeline (Musk: long, flat start to the S-curve)
Valuation regime: ~195x forward P/E leaves the stock very sensitive to narrative and rates
reasoning: Starting point: TSLA at $372 is down ~27% YTD after a 26% July drop following a Q2 2026 miss. Revenue was a record $28.2B (+26%) and deliveries a record 480k, but non-GAAP EPS was $0.33 vs ~$0.54 expected, operating margin 1.4%, FCF -$1.1B on $5.8B capex, and 2026 capex is guided above $25B with FCF negative in coming quarters. Autonomy is moving from concept to early commercialization: paid Cybercab rides in Austin since Sept 3, robotaxi in 7 metros, 1.48M paid FSD subscriptions, FSD approved in 7 EU countries with an EU vote Oct 6. NHTSA opened an audit of Cybercab certification the same day paid rides began. Consensus 2026 EPS is ~$1.77 and 2027 about $2.68 (implied by a 139x 2027 P/E). Analyst targets average ~$397 (median ~$407, range $125-$600, 21 Buy/19 Hold/5 Sell). My SOTP gives ~$307-320: roughly $80/sh for auto+energy, $30/sh for FSD, and ~$190/sh of probability-weighted robotaxi/Optimus optionality. So the price is modestly above fundamental value, while the analyst consensus sits slightly above the price. I set the median 12-month outcome at ~$365, a touch below spot, balancing mild overvaluation and FCF burn against real autonomy momentum and a merger/AI-narrative right tail. For dispersion I used a lognormal with sigma ~0.50, somewhat above the 46% realized vol because of binary events (NHTSA outcome, SpaceX merger, EU/China FSD). I made the right tail slightly fatter to reflect TSLA's history of narrative-driven re-ratings. The scenario-weighted mean is ~$385 (bear $220 at 25%, base $360 at 50%, bull $600 at 25%), consistent with the ladder, which puts P(>=372) at 0.49, P(>=502) at 0.26 and P(<260) at 0.25. Research was ~14 web searches and fetches; no options data consulted.
